title: Real-time Sports Pick'em Platform
tagline: Live player-stat ingestion, entry settlement and payouts for a high-traffic fantasy sports product.
problem: Fans build pick'em entries on live games. Stats arrive from multiple third-party sports data providers with different IDs and formats, and entries must settle correctly and fast once games finish.
built: Ingestion services that normalize player, team and game data across sports data providers
Cross-provider team & player mapping so every stat lands on the right entry
Event-driven settlement pipeline that grades entries as games go final
Internal admin tooling for ops to monitor and correct data
diagram:
flowchart LR
  P[Sports data providers] --> I[Ingestion & mapping]
  I --> K[(Kafka)]
  K --> S[Settlement service]
  S --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
  A[Mobile & web apps] --> API[NestJS API] --> DB
  API --> R[(Redis cache)]
impact: Reliable, automated settlement instead of manual grading
Provider-agnostic data layer, so adding a new sport or provider is config, not a rewrite

title: Collectible Card Pack Platform
tagline: Digital pack openings backed by real, physical trading cards, from inventory to the shipping queue.
problem: Users buy and open packs online, but every card they pull is a real physical item that has to be tracked, valued and eventually shipped.
built: Pack-opening flow with server-side, auditable outcomes
Inventory model linking each digital pull to a physical card
Back-office screens for inventory, packs and ship queues
diagram:
flowchart LR
  U[User] --> W[React app] --> API[Node API]
  API --> O[Pack-open engine]
  O --> INV[(Inventory DB)]
  INV --> SHIP[Ship queue]
  ADM[Admin panel] --> API
impact: A fun, instant digital experience on top of a real-world supply chain
Full audit trail from pack purchase to shipped card

title: AI Knowledge Assistant (RAG)
tagline: A chat assistant that answers questions from private company documents, with sources.
problem: Teams lose time hunting through docs, wikis and PDFs for answers that already exist somewhere.
built: Document ingestion & chunking pipeline into a Pinecone vector index
Retrieval-augmented generation with LangChain + OpenAI, returning cited sources
diagram:
flowchart LR
  D[Docs & PDFs] --> C[Chunk + embed] --> V[(Pinecone)]
  Q[User question] --> R[Retriever] --> V
  R --> L[OpenAI LLM] --> A[Answer + sources]
impact: Answers in seconds instead of searching manually
Grounded responses with links back to the original source

title: Event-driven Microservices Backbone
tagline: Splitting a monolith into independently deployable services talking over queues.
problem: A growing monolith made every release risky and every slow job block user requests.
built: Service boundaries and message contracts over RabbitMQ / Kafka
Background workers for heavy jobs with retries and dead-letter queues
diagram:
flowchart LR
  GW[API gateway] --> S1[Orders svc]
  GW --> S2[Users svc]
  S1 -- events --> MQ[(RabbitMQ / Kafka)]
  MQ --> W[Workers]
  MQ --> S3[Notifications svc]
impact: Slow work moved off the request path
